newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia palm olein stable in late trade.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia palm olein stable in late trade.

text.p: Indonesian palm olein prices were mostly stable in late trading on Monday, with demand improving following gains in Malaysia, traders said.
They said palm olein was quoted at 1,365-70 rupiah/kg in Jakarta, unchanged from the opening, but trades were also heard at five rupiah above and below the range.

"Demand was a little better after prices started rising in Malaysia," one trader said. "Players are waiting for the crop data from PORLA (Malaysia's Palm Oil Registration and Licensing Authority) expected on Tuesday."
Malaysian crop forecaster Ivan Wong estimated the country's June output at 788,000 tonnes against 790,640 in May.
He put end-June stocks at 795,000 tonnes against 711,841 tonnes at end-May, while exports were seen at 595,000 tonnes in June, compared with 626,606 tonnes in May.
"The data was friendly," one trader said. "Production seems to have been rather flat in June."

The traders said volatility in the Indonesian currency had no immediate impact on the market. The rupiah fell sharply early on Monday after regional currency turbulence spilled over to Indonesia, and remained volatile until the afternoon.
"The rupiah's movements have had no impact on the palm oil market," one trader said.
